name: skill-mode-parity
prompt: In this repo, ask the huddle skill to run a research round: "research what competing AI-native SDLC tools do about human gates, with sources". The agent must load the matching mode file and follow it.
origin: 2026-10 port of the Python huddle skill to Go. The legacy skill routed six modes (discussion, research, spec-review, planning, verification, wrap-up); only three were carried into skills/. `grep -ri research skills/` returned nothing, so every research request silently fell back to the generic discussion flow, and nobody noticed because no check compared the router's mode list with the files on disk.

checks.why: Every mode the SKILL.md router names must exist as a file. This is the check that was missing.
checks.run: for m in $(grep -oE 'modes/[a-z-]+\.md' skills/huddle/SKILL.md | sort -u); do test -f "skills/huddle/$m" || { echo "MISSING skills/huddle/$m"; exit 1; }; done

checks.why: Reverse direction: a mode file nobody routes to is dead weight and will drift.
checks.run: for f in skills/huddle/modes/*.md; do grep -q "modes/$(basename $f)" skills/huddle/SKILL.md || { echo "UNROUTED $f"; exit 1; }; done

checks.why: Legacy parity: each mode the Python skill supported is either present or recorded as deliberately dropped in an ADR.
checks.run: for m in discussion research spec-review planning verification wrap-up; do test -f "skills/huddle/modes/$m.md" || grep -rqi "$m" docs/adr/ || { echo "DROPPED WITHOUT A RECORD: $m"; exit 1; }; done

checks.expect: The agent reads skills/huddle/modes/research.md (not modes/discussion.md) before the first persona speaks.
No turn invents a research procedure that is not in the mode file.
